newsitem.title: TURKEY: Motorola, Turkey's Telsim sign $90 million deal.
newsitem.headline: Motorola, Turkey's Telsim sign $90 million deal.

text.p: Motorola Corp. and Turkish wireless operator Telsim said Tuesday they signed a $90 million contract to double Telsim's market share in Turkey by the end of 1997.
The companies also agreed to expand the investment to $160 million later to triple Telsim's line capacity.
Motorola will initially build 500 new digital wireless stations for Telsim in 1997, and another 250 stations when the investment is expanded.
"Our target is to increase our market share to 50 percent from a current 25 percent," Nur Sakarya, Telsim board member, told a news conference.
Telsim had a market share of 45 percent to 50 percent before a conflict emerged with competitor Turk Telekom, he said. The dispute was resolved in early July.
"Our total investment excluding the licence fee will reach $1 billion by the year 2010," Sakarya said, adding that Telsim would begin to post profits in three or four years.
Telsim is owned by Rumeli Holding, which is run by the Uzan family. The other digital wireless operator in Turkey is Turkcell.
Motorola's stock gained 25 cents to $56.625 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
